The '''Ryloth Ark''' was a chest-shaped artifact originally located on [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]], the [[Homeworld/Legends|home]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'leks]]. Around [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], [[Separatist Council/Legends|Separatist Council]] member [[Emir/Legends|Emir]] [[Wat Tambor/Legends|Wat Tambor]] seized control of Ryloth. One of Tambor's tasks was to collect valuables stored on the planet, one of which was the Ark. During a [[Battle of Ryloth/Legends|battle]] on the planet, the Ark was carried by two [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'leks]], as they boarded a [[Sheathipede-class transport shuttle/Legends|''Sheathipede''-class shuttle]]. Years later, in [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]], the Ark was kept inside a display case on Scardia Station, where it was viewed by many, although it was uncertain whether it was the genuine Ark retrieved from the Separatists or a copy.

==Characteristics==
Essentially, the Ryloth Ark was a rectangular, oblong chest plated with [[Gold/Legends|gold]]. Covering the box was a golden lid adorned with two sculptures of winged [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'leks]], [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] [[Alien/Legends|non-Humans]] with two [[Lekku/Legends|"brain tails"]] emerging from the back of their head. The two Twi'leks faced one another, and their wings, which wrapped around their bodies, touched between them. On the bottom of the box, four gold rings were attached, through which two [[Staff/Legends|staves]] could be put, allowing a duo to carry the Ark.<ref name="LOR" />

At least two Arks existed, with one falling down a crevasse on Ryloth.<ref name="LOR" />

==History==
[[File:ScardiaTreasureRoom-LCotJp44.png|thumb|left|The treasure display on Scardia Station]]
As its name suggests, the Ryloth Ark originated on [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]], a rocky [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] inhabited by the Twi'leks.<ref name="LOR" /> Throughout history, several replicas of that artifact were crafted,<ref name="SPINblog">{{SW|url=news/the-star-wars-spy-game-spin-declassified|text=The ''Star Wars'' Spy Game: SPIN Declassified|int=The Star Wars Spy Game: SPIN Declassified|nolive=1}}</ref> and the Ark became the focus of ''[[Piethet Brighteyes and the raiders of the Ryloth Ark]]'', a popular work of fiction that gave dreams of adventures to young boys such as [[Treuten Teradoc|Treuten]] and [[Kosh Teradoc]] from [[Er'Kit/Legends|Er'Kit]].<ref name="Warlords">{{SW|url=news/the-imperial-warlords-despoilers-of-an-empire-part-2|series=The Imperial Warlords: Despoilers of an Empire|text=Part 2|nolive=1}}</ref> During the pan-[[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] conflict known as the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the Ark fell prey to the cupidity of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]&mdash;an affiliation of worlds that had seceded from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and waged war against it. Around [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], the [[Skakoan/Legends|Skakoan]] [[Emir/Legends|Emir]] [[Wat Tambor/Legends|Wat Tambor]] invaded Ryloth in the name of the Confederacy. While the Republic's [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army]] launched an [[Battle of Ryloth/Legends|attack]] to liberate the planet, Tambor raided the vaults of the Twi'leks and had many priceless artifacts loaded on board his personal shuttle. The Ark was one of them, and it was taken away by [[TA-175/Legends|TA-175]], Tambor's [[T-series tactical droid/Legends|tactical droid]], even as he left his master behind.<ref name="LOR" /> The Republic ultimately won the Clone Wars, and its [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] declared a [[Galactic Empire/Legends|New Order]], anointing himself [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref>

In [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]], twenty-seven years after the Battle of Ryloth, it appeared the Ark was in the possession of the [[Church of the Dark Side]],<ref name="TLCOTJ">''[[The Lost City of the Jedi]]''</ref> a charade religion established by the [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence]] following the [[Death/Legends|death]] of Palpatine.<ref name="SPINblog" /> The so-called [[Prophets of the Dark Side]] kept it in a [[Glass/Legends|glass]]-walled display case on [[Scardia Station]], along with a rare set of blood-red [[Mandalorian armor/Legends|Mandalorian armor]]. However, it remained uncertain whether the Prophets owned the genuine article&mdash;retrieved from the long-defunct Separatists&mdash;or a mere copy.<ref name="SPINblog" /> Regardless of its authenticity, the Ark owned by the Church of the Dark Side was lost when [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Afsheen Makati]] destroyed Scardia Station.<ref name="WWGA">{{InsiderCite|66|Who's Who: Imperial Grand Admirals}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:R2C3PO_Ark.jpg|thumb|230px|[[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] and [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] near the Ark (as hieroglyphs) in ''Raiders of the Lost Ark'']]
The Ryloth Ark first appeared in "[[Liberty on Ryloth]]," the twenty-first episode in [[The Clone Wars: Season One|season one]] of the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series. It was inspired by the real-life religious artifact known as the [[Wikipedia:Ark of the Covenant|Ark of the Covenant]].<ref name="CWGuide">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode021.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Liberty on Ryloth}}</ref> According to the [[Wikipedia:Tanakh|Jewish Tanakh]] and the Bible, the Ark of the Covenant was a wooden chest plated with gold in which the stone tablets inscribed with the [[Wikipedia:Ten Commandments|Ten Commandments]] were housed.<ref name="RA">{{WebCite|url=http://jewishencyclopedia.com/articles/1777-ark-of-the-covenant|text=Ark of the Covenant|work=Jewish Encyclopedia|archivedate=20200601044505}}</ref>

A famed, long-lost artifact in real life, the Ark was the focus of the first [[Indiana Jones]] movie, titled ''Raiders of the Lost Ark''. Since ''Star Wars'' creator [[George Lucas]] also produced the [[Indiana Jones (franchise)|''Indiana Jones'' franchise]], the Ryloth Ark was added into ''The Clone Wars'' as an homage.<ref name="SWi">{{InsiderCite|111|Ask Lobot}}</ref>

In the "[[Ask Lobot]]" feature of [[Star Wars Insider 111|''Star Wars Insider'' 111]], the Keeper of the [[Holocron continuity database]], [[Leland Chee]], declared that the Ark of the Covenant's presence in "Liberty on Ryloth" was just "a fun [[Easter egg (virtual)|Easter egg]] to look for" and not meant to be part of the ''Star Wars'' continuity.<ref name="SWi" /> However, the artifact has been explicitly brought into [[Star Wars Legends|the Legends continuity]] by authors [[Greg Mitchell]] and [[Abel G. Peña]], who mentioned the Ryloth Ark and its numerous copies in ''[[The Star Wars Spy Game: SPIN Declassified]]'', an article written for the official [[StarWars.com]] blog.<ref name="SPINblog" /> In Part 2 of ''[[The Imperial Warlords: Despoilers of an Empire]]'', another official blog article, Peña also mentioned a work of fiction called ''Piethet Brighteyes and the raiders of the Ryloth Ark''.<ref name="Warlords" />
